correctness.rationale: For fixed interior finite atoms, log-likelihood lines have strictly increasing slopes and adjacent KL bisectors, yielding Voronoi posterior hardening. The binomial LLN and a triangular-array CLT give fixed-position and \(n^{-1/2}\)-boundary limits. A two-binomial overlap lemma proved via likelihood-ratio crossover, Stirling and geometric tails gives Theta(\(n^{-1/2}\)e^{-nCij}); distinct adjacent atoms dominate the minimal Chernoff rate. The restricted matrix is a reversible positive-semidefinite stochastic Gram operator, and trace/Rayleigh bounds give the sharp norm order. The included checker independently tests exact finite identities and finite numerical asymptotic cases. Assumptions exclude zero/one sites and n-varying support.

value.rationale: Arbitrary-measure Bernstein–Durrmeyer approximation has a natural unresolved incomplete-support regime. For its canonical finite-atomic class, the result supplies the complete off-support limit map and universal Gaussian boundary law, and replaces the general K-functional polynomial recovery bound with a matching exponential Chernoff rate for the actual operator norm. Exact boundary locations and the least-neighbor information determine how an approximation scheme behaves under separated discrete data, useful in approximation and learning from discrete distributions. This is a structural classification with a natural sharp rate, not a single arbitrary parameter computation.
